lessons.title: Life long ago
lessons.canDo: Say what people used to do
lessons.scenario: Smarty, Mia, and Sam visit the city museum and talk about habits from when they were younger.

items.example: I used to walk to school every day.
items.note: Say 'I used to' before a verb to talk about a past habit that is finished now.

items.example: I did not use to drink tea in the morning.
items.note: Use 'I did not use to' without a d on 'use' when something was not true in the past.

items.example: Did you use to play football after school?
items.note: Ask 'Did you use to...?' to find out about someone's past habits.

items.example: When I was younger, I used to watch TV every Saturday.
items.note: Add 'when I was younger' to show the time in your past when a habit happened.

items.example: I used to ride a bike, but I go by bus these days.
items.note: Use 'these days' to contrast your life now with your life in the past.

items.example: Nowadays, we send a message on a phone every day.
items.note: Say 'nowadays' at the start or end of a sentence to talk about the present time.

grammar.title: used to for past habits
grammar.explanation: Use 'used to' plus a base verb for habits or states in the past that are different now. In negatives and questions with 'did', drop the -d and write 'use to'.
examples: I used to read every night.
I did not use to like soup.
Did you use to live near the park?

practice.prompt: Smarty talks about a habit from the past that he stopped. Which phrase fits?
practice.explanation: Use 'I used to' for a repeated action in the past that is finished now.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose what you heard.
practice.audio: I did not use to drink tea.
practice.answer: I did not use to drink tea.
options: I did not use to drink tea.
Did you use to drink tea?
practice.explanation: After 'did not', use 'use to' without a final d.

practice.prompt: Ask Sam about his past habits. Complete the question.
practice.text: ___ play tennis at school?
practice.explanation: Questions with 'Did' use 'use to' without the letter d.

practice.prompt: Match the time expressions with their meaning.
practice.explanation: 'When I was younger' points to the past, while 'these days' and 'nowadays' point to now.

practice.prompt: Build the sentence about Mia's childhood habit.
practice.answer: When I was younger I used to draw.
practice.explanation: Start with 'When I was younger' to set the past time, followed by 'I used to draw'.

practice.prompt: Contrast the past with the present. Complete the sentence.
practice.text: I used to ride a bike, but I take the train ___.
practice.explanation: 'These days' shows what you do now compared with the past.

practice.prompt: Talk about life in the present time. Complete the sentence.
practice.text: ___, we study on a laptop every day.
practice.explanation: 'Nowadays' means in the present time.

practice.prompt: Say the sentence aloud. You can try again.
practice.text: I did not use to like fish, but I like it these days.
practice.answer: I did not use to like fish, but I like it these days.
practice.explanation: 'I did not use to' describes the past, and 'these days' describes now.

story.hook: What did Sam use to do when he was younger?

image.describe: Smarty the black cat, Mia, and Sam standing inside a bright museum hall beside old stone columns and glass cases.

lines.speaker: Smarty

lines.speaker: Sam

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: And what about these days, Sam?

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: Nowadays, I love history! It is my favourite subject.

mission.setup: Smarty asks you about your habits when you were younger and your life nowadays. Answer in your own words.

turns.smarty: When I was younger, I used to sleep all day! Did you use to play a sport or draw?
accept: ^(?:yes )?(?:when i was younger )?i used to (?:play football|play tennis|play basketball|swim|run|draw|paint|dance|sing|read|ride a bike)(?: every day)?$
^no i did not use to (?:play football|play tennis|play basketball|swim|run|draw|paint|dance|sing|read|ride a bike)$
turns.example: When I was younger, I used to play football.
turns.hint: Say 'When I was younger, I used to...' and name an activity.

turns.smarty: What is something you did not use to like when you were younger?
accept: ^(?:when i was younger )?i did not use to like (?:tea|soup|fish|cheese|history|maths|science|reading|homework)$
^i did not use to (?:eat|drink|read|study) (?:tea|soup|fish|cheese|history|maths|science)$
turns.example: I did not use to like tea.
turns.hint: Say 'I did not use to like...' and name a food or subject.

turns.smarty: And what do you enjoy doing these days?
accept: ^(?:these days|nowadays) i (?:like|love|enjoy) (?:history|music|art|science|reading|swimming|running|playing football|playing tennis)$
^i (?:like|love|enjoy) (?:history|music|art|science|reading|swimming|running|playing football|playing tennis) (?:these days|nowadays)$
turns.example: These days, I love music.
turns.hint: Use 'These days' or 'Nowadays' and say what you enjoy.

lessons.title: In the museum
lessons.scenario: Smarty shows Mia and Sam around the main hall of the museum.

items.example: This exhibit is my favourite in the museum.
items.note: Call an object or group of objects shown in a museum an 'exhibit'.

image.describe: Smarty the black cat admiring a painted ancient vase on a pedestal in a museum hall

items.example: The old crown is inside a glass display case.
items.note: A 'display case' is a clear glass box that keeps museum objects safe.

image.describe: a clear glass display case in a museum holding an old silver cup and jewelry

items.example: There is a tall statue next to the museum door.
items.note: Use 'statue' for a figure of a person or animal made from stone or metal.

image.describe: a tall stone statue of a sitting cat on a square base inside a museum

items.example: Look at that small gold ancient coin!
items.note: Say 'ancient coin' for a piece of money from hundreds of years ago.

image.describe: a round gold ancient coin with a stamped owl resting on dark velvet

items.example: I am listening to the audio guide with my headphones.
items.note: An 'audio guide' is a small device that tells you about exhibits as you walk.

image.describe: Mia the cat wearing headphones and holding a small handheld audio guide in a museum

items.example: This statue is on loan from a museum in France.
items.note: Say 'on loan' when an object belongs to another museum and is visiting for a short time.

practice.explanation: A statue is a large figure made from stone or metal.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose what you heard.

practice.answer: The ancient coin is in a display case.

The audio guide is on the table.
The statue is next to the door.

practice.answer: The statue is on loan from Italy.

practice.prompt: Sam puts on his headphones in the museum. Complete the sentence.
practice.text: He is using an ___ to learn about the exhibits.

practice.prompt: Combine Lesson 1 and Lesson 2. Complete the sentence.
practice.text: I ___ think museums were boring, but this exhibit is amazing!
practice.explanation: Use 'used to' for a past belief or habit.

practice.prompt: Say the sentence aloud. You can try again.
practice.text: Look at the ancient coin in the display case.
practice.answer: Look at the ancient coin in the display case.
practice.explanation: Practice saying 'ancient coin' and 'display case' clearly.

story.hook: Where did the tall statue in the gallery come from?

image.describe: Smarty, Mia, and Sam standing in front of a glass display case and a tall stone statue in a museum gallery, with Mia holding an audio guide.

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: My audio guide says this gallery has ten rare exhibits.

lines.speaker: Sam

questions.explanation: Sam says: Look inside this display case! That ancient coin is so small and shiny.

questions.prompt: Why is the statue in the museum?

mission.setup: You are walking through the museum with Smarty. Talk about the objects you see.

turns.smarty: Welcome to the hall! Do you want an audio guide, or are you just looking?
accept: ^(?:i want|i would like|can i have) an audio guide(?: please)?$
^just looking(?: thanks| thank you)?$

turns.smarty: That statue is on loan from Italy. Which exhibit do you like best?

lessons.title: Old and new
lessons.scenario: Smarty, Mia, and Sam compare old objects in the museum with life today.

items.example: Back then, we did not have the internet at home.
items.note: Say 'back then' to refer to a time in the past you were just talking about.

items.example: In those days, journeys by boat took months.
items.note: Use 'in those days' to describe what life was generally like during a past period.

items.example: We used to write letters, but things have changed a lot.
items.note: Say 'things have changed' to show that life now is very different from before.

items.example: We travel by plane much more than before.
items.note: Add 'much more than before' to show something happens a lot more often now.

items.example: I do not play with my old teddy bear any more.
items.note: Put 'not' with the verb and 'any more' at the end to say a habit has stopped.

items.example: As a child, I used to visit my grandmother every summer.
items.note: Use 'as a child' to talk about things you did when you were young.

grammar.title: Comparing past and present
grammar.explanation: Set the past scene with 'back then', 'in those days', or 'as a child'. Then show the change now with 'things have changed', 'much more than before', or 'not ... any more'.
examples: In those days, phones were very big.
I do not watch cartoons any more.

practice.prompt: Smarty talks about life a hundred years ago. Which phrase means 'at that past time'?
practice.explanation: 'Back then' refers to an earlier time in the past.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose what you heard.
practice.audio: In those days, we did not have laptops.
practice.answer: In those days, we did not have laptops.
options: In those days, we did not have laptops.
As a child, I had a laptop.
practice.explanation: 'In those days' introduces how life used to be in the past.

practice.prompt: Mia sees how different life is now. Complete the sentence.
practice.text: Back then there were no phones, so ___.
practice.explanation: Use 'things have changed' to show a big difference between past and present.

practice.prompt: Match the phrases with how we use them.
practice.explanation: Each phrase helps compare what happened before with what happens now.

practice.prompt: Build the sentence comparing travel now and in the past.
practice.answer: We go by plane much more than before.
practice.explanation: 'Much more than before' goes at the end to compare now with the past.

practice.prompt: Sam stopped playing with old toys. Complete the sentence.
practice.text: I do not play in the playground ___.
practice.explanation: Use 'not ... any more' to show a past habit has ended.

practice.prompt: Talk about your early years. Complete the sentence.
practice.text: ___, I used to read in bed every evening.
practice.explanation: 'As a child' sets the time when you were young.

practice.prompt: Say the sentence aloud. You can try again.
practice.text: Things have changed, and we use computers much more than before.
practice.answer: Things have changed, and we use computers much more than before.
practice.explanation: Great job comparing the past and present!

story.hook: How did people travel and dress in those days compared with now?

image.describe: Smarty, Mia, and Sam looking at an exhibit showing an old wooden bicycle next to a sleek modern electric scooter in the museum.

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: Look at this exhibit of old fashion and early transport.

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: In those days, the clothes looked so heavy and warm!

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: Nowadays, we have modern trains and planes, so we travel much more than before.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: As a child, I rode a small bicycle, but I do not ride that one any more!

questions.prompt: Why do we travel much more than before?
questions.answer: Because we have new trains and planes.
options: Because we have new trains and planes.
questions.explanation: Mia says we have new trains and planes, so we travel much more than before.

questions.prompt: What does Sam say about his small childhood bicycle?
questions.answer: He does not ride it any more.
options: He does not ride it any more.
questions.explanation: Sam says: I do not ride that one any more!

mission.setup: Smarty asks you to compare your life as a child with your life now. Answer in your own words.

turns.smarty: As a child, what did you use to do every weekend?
accept: ^(?:as a child )?i used to (?:play football|play tennis|watch tv|read|swim|draw|ride a bike|visit my grandmother|visit my grandfather)(?: every weekend)?$
turns.example: As a child, I used to watch TV.
turns.hint: Start with 'As a child, I used to...' and name an activity.

turns.smarty: Do you still do that, or not any more?
accept: ^(?:i do )?not(?: do that)? any more$
^no i do not(?: do that)? any more$
^things have changed$
turns.example: I do not do that any more.
turns.hint: Say 'I do not do that any more' or 'Things have changed'.

turns.smarty: In those days, we did not have fast internet. What do you use much more than before?
accept: ^i use (?:my phone|my laptop|my computer|the internet|apps) much more than before$
^we use (?:phones|laptops|computers|the internet) much more than before$
turns.example: I use my phone much more than before.
turns.hint: Say 'I use my phone much more than before' or name another device.

lessons.title: My grandparents
lessons.scenario: Mia and Sam look at a family history exhibit in the museum and talk about their grandparents.

items.example: My grandparents worked on a farm when they were young.
items.note: Use 'when they were young' to talk about your parents' or grandparents' youth.

items.example: In their day, very few families had a car.
items.note: Say 'in their day' to describe the time when older family members were growing up.

items.example: My grandmother grew up in a small village near the river.
items.note: Say 'grew up in' plus a place to tell where someone spent their childhood.

items.example: My grandfather passed away five years ago.
items.note: 'Passed away' is a gentle, polite way to say that someone died.

items.example: Families often hand down old watches and books to their children.
items.note: Use 'hand down' when older family members give special objects to younger ones.

items.example: We drew a family tree to show our parents and grandparents.
items.note: A 'family tree' is a chart showing how everyone in a family is related.

practice.prompt: Mia tells where her grandfather lived as a boy. Which phrase fits?
practice.explanation: Use 'grew up in' before a town or country where someone spent childhood.

practice.answer: My grandmother lived in England when she was young.

My grandmother lives in England these days.
My parents grew up in Brazil.
practice.explanation: 'When they were young' describes the time of their youth.

practice.prompt: Match the family history phrases with their meanings.
practice.explanation: These phrases help describe family history across generations.

practice.prompt: Talk about the era when your grandparents were young. Complete the sentence.
practice.text: ___, children walked to school in the snow.

practice.explanation: 'Passed away' is a gentle way to say someone died.

practice.answer: Parents hand down treasures to their children.

practice.prompt: Mia draws a chart of her relatives. Complete the sentence.
practice.text: We made ___ for our history homework.
practice.explanation: A family tree shows parents, grandparents, aunts, and uncles.

practice.prompt: Say the sentence aloud. You can try again.
practice.text: My grandmother grew up in Uzbekistan when they were young.
practice.answer: My grandmother grew up in Uzbekistan when they were young.
practice.explanation: Well done describing where your family came from!

lessons.title: Before that
lessons.scenario: Smarty, Mia, and Sam talk about what had happened before they arrived at the museum.

items.example: I had already bought the tickets before Sam arrived.
items.note: Use 'I had already' plus a past participle to show an action finished earlier than another past event.

items.example: By the time we arrived, the museum had already opened.
items.note: Say 'by the time' before a past event to show something else happened before that moment.

items.example: The rain had not yet stopped when we left home.
items.note: Use 'had not yet' plus a past participle when something had not happened before a past moment.

items.example: After I had read the map, I found the right gallery.
items.note: Use 'after I had' plus a past participle to put two past actions in clear order.

items.example: Smarty had already got the audio guides before we arrived.
items.note: Use 'before we arrived' with the past simple to mark the later point in the past.

items.example: Mia was excited because she had never seen a real ancient coin.
items.note: Use 'she had never seen' to talk about a first-time experience in the past.

grammar.title: Past perfect: had + past participle
grammar.explanation: Use 'had' plus a past participle for the earlier of two past actions, and the past simple for the later action. Words like 'already', 'never', 'by the time', 'after', and 'before' make the order clear.
examples: I had already bought the tickets before we arrived.
She had never seen an ancient coin.
By the time we arrived, the visit had not yet started.

practice.prompt: Which action happened FIRST? 'I had already eaten breakfast before Sam came.'
practice.explanation: 'I had already eaten' is in the past perfect, so it happened before Sam came.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose what you heard.
practice.audio: She had never seen a statue so big.
practice.answer: She had never seen a statue so big.
options: She had never seen a statue so big.
She has never seen a statue.
She used to see a big statue.
practice.explanation: 'She had never seen' describes a first-time experience in the past.

practice.prompt: Connect the two past events. Complete the sentence.
practice.text: ___ we arrived at the station, the train had already left.
practice.explanation: Use 'By the time' before the later past event ('we arrived').

practice.prompt: The museum doors were still closed when they got there. Complete the sentence.
practice.text: The museum ___ opened when we arrived.

lessons.title: Mission: Museum guide
lessons.canDo: Tell a visitor how life changed
lessons.scenario: You become a junior museum guide alongside Smarty and explain how life has changed from then to now.

practice.prompt: Choose the right phrase to describe a past habit.
practice.text: When I was younger, I ___ visit the museum every Sunday.
practice.explanation: Use 'used to' for a repeated habit in the past.

practice.prompt: Match the Unit 4 words with their meanings.
practice.explanation: Each phrase comes from a key topic in Unit 4.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose what you heard.
practice.audio: By the time we arrived, the guided visit had already started.
practice.answer: By the time we arrived, the guided visit had already started.
options: By the time we arrived, the guided visit had already started.
In those days, we took a guided visit.
It turned out that the palace was closed.
practice.explanation: Listen for 'By the time we arrived', 'guided visit', and 'had already'.

practice.prompt: Complete the comparison between past and present.
practice.text: In those days, letters took weeks, so ___ a lot.
practice.explanation: 'Things have changed' highlights the contrast between then and now.

practice.prompt: Build the sentence explaining the museum discovery.
practice.answer: It turned out that the coin was ancient.
practice.explanation: 'It turned out that' introduces the surprising discovery.

practice.prompt: Complete the sentence about grandparents.
practice.text: My grandparents ___ a small town and handed down many photos.
practice.explanation: 'Grew up in' tells where someone spent their childhood.

practice.prompt: Say the sentence aloud. You can try again.
practice.text: Nowadays, we no longer use ancient coins, and things have changed much more than before.
practice.answer: Nowadays, we no longer use ancient coins, and things have changed much more than before.
practice.explanation: You mastered the language of Unit 4!

story.hook: How well can Mia and Sam guide visitors through the Then & Now gallery?

image.describe: Smarty wearing a tiny bow tie while Mia and Sam hold audio guides and lead visitors past a statue, an old bridge model, and framed black and white photos.

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: Today is our guided visit! Let's show our guests how life changed from then to now.

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: Look at this black and white photo in the frame. In those days, people used to travel by horse.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: Yes, horses gave way to trains and planes, and old tools were replaced by machines.

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: Over here is a statue from a fortress built in 1400. At that time, it protected the whole palace.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: Before we arrived at this gallery, I had never seen an ancient coin so clear!

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: It turned out that you two make amazing museum guides! Things have changed for the better.

questions.prompt: What did horses give way to according to Sam?
questions.explanation: Sam says: horses gave way to trains and planes.

questions.prompt: When was the fortress built?
questions.explanation: Mia says the statue is from a fortress built in 1400.

mission.setup: You are the museum guide! Welcome Smarty, show an exhibit, and explain how life has changed.

turns.smarty: Hello, guide! Welcome me to the exhibit and tell me what we can see.
accept: ^(?:hello|welcome)(?: smarty)? (?:here is|we have|you can see) (?:an ancient coin|a statue|a black and white photo|an exhibit|a palace)$
^(?:here is|this is) (?:an ancient coin|a statue|a black and white photo|an exhibit)$
turns.example: Hello, Smarty! Here is an ancient coin.
turns.hint: Welcome Smarty and point out an exhibit, statue, ancient coin, or black and white photo.

turns.smarty: How did people use to live back then compared with nowadays?
accept: ^back then people used to (?:walk|ride a bike|write letters|work on a farm) but nowadays things have changed$
^in those days we did not have phones but nowadays things have changed$
^things have changed and we use phones much more than before$
turns.example: In those days, we did not have phones, but nowadays things have changed.
turns.hint: Compare 'back then' or 'in those days' with 'nowadays' or 'things have changed'.

turns.smarty: What happened to the old ways and tools from that era?
accept: ^they were replaced by (?:new tools|machines|computers|phones)$
^they (?:died out|went out of fashion|fell apart)$
^old tools gave way to (?:machines|computers)$
turns.example: They were replaced by machines.
turns.hint: Use 'replaced by', 'gave way to', 'died out', or 'went out of fashion'.

episode.title: The Hidden Door in the Museum

panels.speaker: Smarty
panels.text: By the time the last visitors left the museum, the sky outside had already turned dark.

image.describe: Smarty the black cat standing near tall museum windows as twilight falls outside.

panels.speaker: Mia
panels.text: Look behind that tall statue! There is a small wooden box that was not there earlier.

panels.speaker: Sam
panels.text: It looks very old and faded. It had been hidden behind the display case for a century!

panels.speaker: Smarty
panels.text: Inside is a black and white photo of an ancient fortress, plus a silver memento.

image.describe: An open wooden keepsake box showing a faded black and white photo of a fortress and a gleaming silver key.

panels.speaker: Mia
panels.text: Look in the background of the photo! There is a secret door under the old bridge.

panels.speaker: Sam
panels.text: And it turned out that this silver memento is actually a key!

panels.speaker: Smarty
panels.text: I had never seen a key like this before. Let's walk down to the basement gallery and try the lock!

image.describe: Smarty, Mia, and Sam holding a lantern and the silver key in front of an old stone door in the museum basement.

questions.prompt: Where had the wooden box been hidden?
questions.explanation: Sam says the box had been hidden behind the display case.

questions.prompt: What did it turn out that the silver memento really was?
questions.explanation: Sam discovers that the silver memento is actually a key.
